description: Hub-mode enumeration and DMA-batched OCP recovery.
success definition: Hub and both devices enumerate correctly. Host observes Recovery Mode before PROT_CAP. Device0 exposes valid OCP descriptors and capabilities, delivers the image exactly once and in order to AXI, and accepts activation with a fresh register-visible transition and correct status readback.
status: Done; functional 4/252/256/520B seeds4/3/2/1; waveform verified; OCP_CAP_INDIRECT_CTRL; ref 20261106.211107

description: OCP and non-OCP control traffic on device0 EP0.
success definition: Completed requests return correct data. Replacement SETUP supersedes the old control transfer; subsequent responses belong only to the new request. Accepted FIFO data is neither lost nor duplicated, and OCP recovery completes.
status: Done; DUT prefix-loss deadlock (4/252/520B); DMA/activation/drain unreached; OCP_CAP_INDIRECT_CTRL; ref 20261107.014904

description: Device0 OCP overlapped with device0 bulk, interrupt, or isochronous traffic.
success definition: Non-EP0 transactions occur within an active OCP transfer window. Both paths preserve payload and endpoint identity; bulk retries, interrupt service, and isochronous frame delivery follow their respective rules. OCP completes without corruption or starvation.
status: Done; BULK520B/INT4B/ISO252B seeds1/2/3; waveform/controls/preservation verified; OCP_CAP_INDIRECT_CTRL; ref 20261107.061131

description: Device0 OCP overlapped with device1 control traffic.
success definition: Device1 control transactions occur while device0 OCP is active. Each device returns its own requested data and completes its control stages without cross-device state, payload, or address contamination.
status: Done; functional 4/252/520B seeds2/3/1; waveform verified; OCP_CAP_INDIRECT_CTRL; ref 20261107.000546

description: Device0 OCP overlapped with device1 bulk, interrupt, or isochronous traffic.
success definition: Device1 non-EP0 transactions occur within an active OCP transfer window. Both devices deliver correct payloads with transfer-type-correct retry and periodic behavior; OCP completes without cross-device corruption or starvation.

description: OCP, device0 non-OCP EP0/EPN, and device1 EPN traffic.
success definition: Observed transactions demonstrate the requested interleaving while AXI actors service both devices. EP0 replacement is correct; every endpoint preserves data and transfer-type semantics; OCP finishes without deadlock or cross-stream contamination.

description: L2 global and selective-port suspend during image recovery.
success definition: USB address/configuration and pending recovery state survive suspend, accounting for AXI consumption. Resume introduces no lost/duplicated data. Suspended segments remain idle; the other device progresses during selective suspend. Both modes are exercised with recovery in progress.

description: USB bus and downstream-port resets during image push/activation.
success definition: Before firmware reinitialization, FIFO data/indices, recovery status and activation match the approved reset-scope contract. Affected devices reset and re-enumerate; OCP discovery and a fresh image transfer succeed without stale responses. Port resets preserve the other device, including device0 recovery during device1 reset. Cover bus and both port resets with partial images.

description: Device0 OCP and device1 EPN traffic through a native full-speed hub.
success definition: Hub and devices enumerate at full speed. OCP and device1 transactions interleave with legal FS packet sizes and periodic scheduling; bulk/interrupt and isochronous delivery obey their distinct rules, with no data corruption.

description: Injected OCP protocol STALL crossed with non-OCP traffic.
success definition: The selected error produces the expected EP0 STALL and read-to-clear OCP error status. Legal control-pipe recovery restores mandatory OCP commands; independent non-OCP traffic stays correct, with no stale response or unintended side effect.

description: FIFO-full OCP NAKs interleaved with device0 non-OCP EP0.
success definition: FIFO accepts its full advertised depth but never overruns. Non-OCP SETUP replaces the blocked OCP transfer correctly; after drain and legal OCP resubmission, accepted image bytes remain ordered and unique and both request types complete.

description: FIFO-full OCP NAKs crossed with non-EP0 traffic.
success definition: Full FIFO NAKs do not stall independent bulk, interrupt, or isochronous service. AXI drain releases backpressure and OCP progresses without overflow, loss, or duplicate acceptance; non-EP0 payloads and periodic delivery remain correct.
